items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: I was happy to jump to that group because I could do what I wanted to... Charlie Miller's bands.

ctx.x: Before Charlie Miller. I played with another group at the Waltz Dream. That was a very, very popular dancing, dance hall, Negro dance hall. See, I played at this Waltz Dream, and with this, with this - which I forget the name of this band now, right now. Anyway, it was a very, very popular dance hall, where everybody, particularly Saturday nights it was packed. And they, the driver, it was a trommel [?], and it was Charlie Miller to me. You know how this - it changed the way that I recommended Jabbo to Charlie…

seemed to be doing the things that I wanted to do: play jazz, take solos, a whole lot of solos, as long as I want, you know. That's what Charlie used to let us do, 'cause everybody liked to play jazz, you know. So that's why I bring it up all the time about Charlie, Charlie Miller's bands.
OK, some questions about that. When you say 'take solos', would they be solos the way we recognize jazz solos now? Were they melody reshapings or were they -

items.title: Benny Waters interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: I heard him in Kansas City with Jay McShann... I give Charlie the credit of changing the scene in alto playing.

ctx.x: How did he change the way that alto sax players played?

Well Charlie gets credit for that see? Of pioneering in a new style. Firstly, I’ve heard Benny Carter play so much when he was young, see? And I always thought Benny was a pioneer also. He started at, particularly at that period. But I give Charlie the credit of changing the scene in alto playing. But you know he did most of that when he arrived in New York. I heard him in Kansas City with Jay McShann. He wasn’t playing exactly the same way. He was still, you could hear edges of his style coming out, but it…
If you, after all your many years of experience, if you could leave today’s music scene in our young and upcoming students —
